change: Moved 'glutes' (Gluteus Maximus) from secondary to primary. In high-knee running, the gluteus maximus is a prime mover driving hip extension with each stride — EMG research on running confirms high glute activation as a primary contributor. Also moved Hamstrings from secondary to first secondary position (they assist and stabilize during running) and removed abs from secondary (core bracing role is minor enough on this dynamic running movement compared to the listed primaries; hamstrings are a more meaningful secondary). Abductor retained as primary for hip flexor drive of the knee lift.

Moved 'glutes' (Gluteus Maximus) from secondary to primary. Research on tuck/knee jumps confirms glutes are primary movers during takeoff (hip extension) and landing absorption — comparable role to quads. Abs retained as primary because actively pulling knees to chest is a defining feature of this exercise. Removed 'Abductor' from secondary (hip flexor contribution in this bilateral tuck movement is minor compared to the main movers) and kept Hamstrings as secondary (assist in tuck phase knee flexion and landing control).
